Read more More than 280,000 people have been forced to flee their homes as devastating wildfires rage across central Spain and southwestern France. High winds have left firefighters struggling to battle flames as Spain declared a national emergency, with multiple fires merging outside Madrid. France has deployed its army, with hundreds of soldiers joining efforts to contain the flames , which have ripped through a record 98,000 hectares since January. On Saturday, authorities ordered the evacuation of large parts of Bordeaux ’s suburbs, including the areas of Le Haillan, Eysines ​and Merignac. “The fires ‌which are hitting our country have reached a level that has never ​been seen before,” French ‌prime minister Sebastien Lecornu wrote on X on Saturday. Madrid’s regional president, Isabel Diaz Ayuso, said it was the “worst fire in the history of the region” and that conditions had been made worse by a combination of high temperatures, wind, and the merging of a number of fires. open image in gallery Firefighters near Lacanau, southwestern France ( AP ) European Union countries have sent helicopters, planes and ground teams. These include 40 personnel from a Romanian forest fire team, two Portuguese and two Swedish Air Tractor planes, four helicopters – including two from Germany, one from the Czech Republic and one from Slovakia – and from Switzerland, four light helicopters and 30 ground personnel. “Europe stands alongside France and Spain in the face of the devastating wildfires ravaging them,” European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen wrote in a post on X. Residents forced to evacuate have described apocalyptic scenes as they left their homes behind. Marion Girault-Rime was awoken at around 4am on Friday by an emergency alert on her phone that instructed every citizen of the wealthy resort town of Lege-Cap Ferret to evacuate immediately. She grabbed underwear and toothbrushes and, along with her daughter Mahau and boyfriend Tony, rushed to the car. “Luckily, my husband and son were not at home,” she said. open image in gallery Marion Girault-Rime was forced to flee her home in the town of Lege-Cap Ferret ( Marion Girault-Rime/Quatre Histoires ) It was not long until they were overwhelmed by the smell of smoke as they joined hundreds of other cars fleeing the area. Ms Girault-Rime was left speechless as cinders blew across the windscreen as though it was “raining ash”, with bright red flames erupting and a towering pillar of black smoke. The scene was “frightening and spectacular ”, the 53-year-old told The Independent. Colonel Romain Moutard, the deputy director of the Landes fire and rescue service, said the fire was “apocalyptic” and described the situation as “Dante-esque” as the flames spread. The length of the final stage of the Tour de France has been shortened to allow police officers to be redeployed to battle the raging wildfires. The race’s final stage on Sunday will be reduced in length by a third, the Paris police department said, in an extraordinary measure that underscores the gravity of the fires. The UK government is advising citizens in Spain to avoid travelling through affected areas of Madrid and Avila, while those in France are being told to follow the advice of local authorities. Prospective holidaymakers are advised to check with their accommodation or travel provider before making the journey. A French foreign minister urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans. open image in gallery Firefighters from Spain’s military emergencies unit battle flames in El Tiemblo, 80km west of Madrid ( AFP/Getty ) Wildfires are also affecting parts of Scotland, with a major incident declared in the Cairngorms national park. More than 500 firefighters have been tackling the blaze, which has raged for the past 10 days and forced locals from their homes in the remote region. Residents of Nethy Bridge , a Scottish village facing evacuation, are “frustrated” that the fire has not yet been brought under control. “A lot of people are upset, angry and frustrated at the ongoing situation, because the Scottish government said a week ago [on Wednesday] that they had enough resources to deal with it, and they said on Thursday that the fire was contained,” said Sandy McCook, chair of the Nethy Bridge and Vicinity Community Council. “My argument with that is, if you said the fire was contained and you had enough resources last Wednesday and Thursday, why are we still fighting it 10 days later, and it’s still running out of control? It is still not controlled in any way, shape or form.” Mr McCook said that residents of the Cairngorms village could see large plumes of smoke from the wildfire on Friday before they were evacuated. He added: “Apocalyptic is the word for the pall of smoke that was on the go yesterday.” open image in gallery Smoke rises from the wildfire in the Cairngorms national park on Saturday ( PA ) Scotland’s first minister John Swinney has said that the Cairngorms national park wildfire is still a “very serious situation”. “Residents, businesses and people staying in the affected areas will understandably be very worried,” he added. “My thoughts are with them and I thank them for their understanding. “With the fire changing to be in the direction of Nethy Bridge yesterday afternoon, a precautionary evacuation was put in place, and a fire break was successfully established overnight to protect the village. “Police officers visited all properties in Nethy Bridge, and officers are in the village today to support residents. “The wind has changed direction overnight, which means the track of the fire has altered once again, and the threat to Nethy Bridge has reduced, for the moment at least. Ground and helicopter resources are being focused on the current path of the fire, and new fire breaks constructed.” The first minister said such situations can change “very quickly and dramatically”, reflecting the challenges faced by the Scottish Fire and Rescue Services and other responders. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/un-c.text: As the race to elect the next UN Secretary-General enters its final phase, former Costa Rican Vice President Rebeca Grynspan retains a challenging lead, but a new contender is emerging, as UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh announced her candidacy this week.The growing excitement around the race is also fueled by the prospect of a female UN secretary-general, something that has never happened in the UN's more than 80-year history.As part of a complex election process, an informal straw poll of officials in the deciding United Nations Security Council last week gave Grynspan a narrow lead over her closest competitors: Guyana’s former Foreign Minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and Argentina’s International Atomic Energy Agency Director-General Rafael Grossi.But after receiving two opposing votes the race has been relaunched allowing new candidates to participate.The winner needs at least nine votes from the 15-member UN Security Council without opposition from any of the five permanent members — the US, the UK, France, China and Russia — and they have until the end of December to choose the successor to current UN chief Antonio Gutteres, before the UN General Assembly confirms the appointment.Campaigning alongside Grynspan, Grossi and Rodrigues-Birkett are former Ecuadorian Foreign Minister Maria Fernanda Espinosa, Argentina's Rafael Grossi, former Senegalese President Macky Sall, former UN Under-Secretary-General Olara Otunnu of Uganda, and Ecuadorian diplomat Ivonne A-Baki.UAE’s Nusseibeh announced as fresh contender Senior UAE diplomat and UAE Miniaster of State Lana Nusseibeh energised the race when her nomination was announced this week, known for her versatility in “quiet diplomacy” in the campaign for peace and for creating space for wider political settlements. Launching her candidacy, Nusseibeh said, “I have spent much of my professional life working in and around the United Nations, and I have seen first-hand what determined diplomacy can achieve - countries with profound differences finding common ground, and agreement where people said agreement was impossible.”In her vision statement, she puts peace and security at the core while also promising to deliver across the board on development and human rights, as well as reform the organisation around focus and results. "I am standing to be secretary-general because I believe this is a moment to act with greater urgency: to act earlier, bring people together across difference, and drive the work forward until it produces concrete results," she said.“I wish to offer myself to this office as I would serve it: speaking frankly with every government and answering to none.”A highly regarded diplomat who grew up between Abu Dhabi and the UK in a family of well-known political figures, Nusseibeh previously served as the UAE ambassador to the UN and is credited with elevating the UAE's profile during that time.Nusseibeh, 48, who led the UAE’s successful bid for a Security Council seat, said that several countries approached her during the last UN General Assembly and urged her to stand.“It's recognised today that we need someone who offers generational change for the organisation,” she said. During the country’s 2022 to 2023 term, Nusseibeh secured the adoption of Resolution 2720, which opened the way for humanitarian aid deliveries into Gaza. A Hebrew speaker, she said she secured support for the resolution by arranging visits from Council members to the Rafah border crossing. If she succeeds, Nusseibeh would become the first woman to lead the United Nations since its establishment in 1945, the first of Palestinian descent, and the second Secretary-General from the Arabic-speaking world after Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali.“I think ⁠it would be great if the next secretary-general is a woman, but I am not running because I am a woman, I am running because I am stubbornly optimistic about the future of the United Nations and I believe we need someone who is relentless in the pursuit of diplomacy to open doors,” Nusseibeh said on Wednesday.Grynspan holds a challenging leadCosta Rica's former Vice President Rebeca Grynspan, 70, was born to Jewish parents who fled Poland before World War II, and she has built a Jewish family ever since. She lost her grandparents in the Holocaust after they decided to remain in Poland. In a May interview with Euronews, Grynspan said, “I know exactly what wars take away from you and what peace allows you to do.” “I am a generation that have lived in peace. I have never experienced war directly. But millions of people in the world today live in war zones, in conflict. And that is why I am running, because I know the difference, what peace and opportunity can do for you and your family,” she told Euronews.Currently Secretary-General of the UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD), Grynspan said she agreed with US President Donald Trump’s “constructive” criticism that “the UN has great potential, but it's not living up to that potential,” and that a reformed UN can make a difference.Grynspan told Euronews how she believes that in our multipolar world “the choice is if we will have multipolarity with multilateralism that bears the promise of prosperity and cooperation, or if we will have multipolarity without multilateralism that will lead us to fragmentation into a world that will be more unstable, more prone to conflict, and less prosper.” “So we need to create again these spaces. For the convergence of divergent interests,” she added.On the other hand, she also hailed the “amazing things that are happening in the world: you look at technology and you look at the digital world, the artificial intelligence, what is happening in medicine and in science.”“You see those breakthroughs that you can bring to the people on the ground, to the millions of people that have right now no opportunity, that live in poverty, in absolute destitution or in hunger.““And you know that the world is developing really the capacity, the possibility for everybody to have a dignified life. That will depend on us. It will depend on our choices,” Grynspan explained in an interview for Euronews.She said that the UN election race was “not like a business-as-usual type of election.”“Conflicts in the world are going up. Trust between the countries, but also in the multilateral system, is going down. And time is running out," Grynspan told Euronews as she presented the vision of her candidacy to become the new UN secretary-general."So this is a moment in which we have to raise to the challenge to bring cooperation, solidarity, the principles of the UN Charter again into the center of the agenda,” she concluded.

WARSAW, Poland (AP) — A woman wounded three people inside an educational institution in Poland's capital, Warsaw, on Saturday, police say, in the third attack at a school in less than a week. Bloodstains were visible Saturday afternoon on a patch of grass near the entrance to the private post-secondary school in the Praga district of Warsaw. The school was open on Saturday and the victims were submitting papers at the school office when they were attacked, police said. The attack came after police on Saturday said they detained 76 people across Poland and checked nearly 50,000 schools nationwide as part of efforts to prevent further violence following two school attacks earlier in the week. The suspect on Saturday used a “dangerous object” to attack a 17-year-old girl and also wounded two other people, aged 17 and 24, Jakub Filipiak, a spokesman for Warsaw police, told The Associated Press. None of the wounds were life-threatening. The suspect was in custody. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student at a vocational school in the Mazovian province in central Poland attacked fellow students, teachers and passersby with a sharp object, wounding nine people. He was arrested nearby. The following day, a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two others in a knife attack at his former school in the same province. The assaults, both carried out by Polish nationals, shocked a country where school violence is a new phenomenon. Police say no evidence the attacks were coordinated So far, the government said it had found no evidence that an internet challenge promoting school attacks was ongoing. There was no official confirmation that the attacks were linked. The attacks “happen one after the other and there is geographic proximity, so you are left wondering if they are not connected,” Kacper Rekawek, senior researcher at the International Center for Counterterrorism in The Hague, told the AP. “This is essentially a copycat scenario, something of a long trail of attackers going back to at least 2019, if not decades earlier,” he said, referring to Brenton Tarrant, the white supremacist who shot and killed 51 Muslims at two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, in 2019. Rekawek said that one of the suspects in the latest attacks used the same imagery and aesthetics as Tarrant, which means the Polish incidents should be “placed within the confines of essentially terrorist behavior.” Rumors that the attacks were coordinated and that there would be more on “bloody Friday” had been shared Thursday night in parents' online groups and by mainstream media. It led to 59 schools preemptively suspending classes on Friday across Poland, the majority in Mazovian province. In other schools, principals sent messages announcing stepped-up security measures including extra staff at entrances and backpack checks. “There will ⁠be no compromise here. The safety of the youth is the most important thing,” Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said. Knives confiscated in schools as violence grows Those detained on Friday include a 14-year-old boy from Warsaw who was found in possession of a knife with a concealed blade and 11 firecrackers, and a 16-year old who came to school with a butterfly knife in his backpack, police said. Others had posted online photos of knives, threatened their peers or threatened school attacks, police said. Parents are now having to catch up fast on how to speak to their kids about school violence. Authorities say extra security measures at schools will continue and crisis training will be organized. The liberal government also promised to renew efforts to pass a bill blocking harmful online content. “If that juvenile attacker had streamed the crime online today, we would have been unable to block that content because we have not been given that legal tool,” Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. After allegedly killing the school custodian and wounding two adults in Thursday’s attack, the 15-year-old, who wore a camera to record his actions, was eventually overpowered by school principal Krzysztof Ochmański. Ochmański later told reporters there was a moment when the boy seemed to realize the enormity of his actions and said he did not want to do this anymore. “Once I had established contact, he asked me for help,” Ochmański recounted. “It got to the point where he wanted a hug.” News Nevada Top stories Investigation underway after human remains found in Churchill County University of Nevada, Reno announces new brand identity, opens fieldhouse at 2026 State of the University Sparks police arrest Reno resident after reported vehicle ramming incident Copyright 2026 The Associated Press.
